Package paint.shared.io.internal

Class SquaresTableIO

java.lang.Object
paint.shared.io.internal.SquaresTableIO
public class SquaresTableIO extends Object
Internal schema-validated table I/O implementation for Square.

Handles low-level I/O and data conversion between PAINT Square objects and Tablesaw Table structures.

The SquaresTableIO class provides implementation for mapping square entity fields to CSV columns and vice versa. It manages the schema specific to "squares.csv" files, ensuring that data types and headers are correctly applied during conversion.

    • newEmptyTable

      protected static <E extends Enum<E>> tech.tablesaw.api.Table newEmptyTable(String tableName, E[] columns, Function<E,String> headerFn, Function<E,tech.tablesaw.api.ColumnType> typeFn)
      Creates a new empty Table whose schema is derived from a column enum. This replaces the per-subclass getColumnHeaders() / getColumnTypes() helpers: each TableIO implementation supplies its Column enum values plus accessors for the header name and column type, and this method assembles the name/type arrays in enum order and delegates to newEmptyTable(String, String[], ColumnType[]).
      Type Parameters:
      E - the column enum type
      Parameters:
      tableName - name of the resulting table
      columns - the schema enum's values, in schema order
      headerFn - extracts the CSV header name from a column value
      typeFn - extracts the ColumnType from a column value
      Returns:
      a new empty Table with the derived schema

    • readCsvWithSchema

      public tech.tablesaw.api.Table readCsvWithSchema(Path csvPath, String[] expectedCols, tech.tablesaw.api.ColumnType[] expectedTypes, boolean allowSuperset) throws IOException
      Reads a CSV file into a Table with a known schema and validates its header and types.

      This implementation uses a two-step import process:

      1. Read the CSV with all columns forced to STRING.
      2. Normalize boolean values and convert types according to the schema.

      This avoids Tablesaw’s strict Boolean parser rejecting values such as "true", "false", "yes", "no", "1", "0", etc.

      Parameters:
      csvPath - path to the CSV file
      expectedCols - expected column names in order
      expectedTypes - expected column types in order
      allowSuperset - if true, allows the CSV to contain extra columns
      Returns:
      a typed, schema-validated Table
      Throws:
      IOException - if the CSV is missing, invalid, or fails validation
